workstream: WS6 — human-anchored judge calibration via /eval-review (proposal V3-2)
summary: Close the criterion-validity loop the harness already has both halves of: /eval-review gains an optional structured-verdicts elicitation (human verdict per judge per case, on the judge's own scale, elicited BEFORE the judge's rationale is revealed), persisted in review.yaml alongside reviewer_id, a blind contamination flag, and the selection basis. A new `score.py calibration` subcommand joins those verdicts against summary.yaml per_case on the case-directory key (reduced values only; null-valued if:-skipped/errored entries excluded), selects the structurally correct metric via WS1's reliability.select_irr_metric (Cohen's kappa for the 2-fixed-rater bool case; Krippendorff's alpha ordinal/interval otherwise), and merges the result into summary['judges'][name]['human_agreement'] so the existing detect_regressions/cmd_regression and report.py agg-read paths can see it (verdict correction #1 — the originally designed top-level calibration block is invisible to the gate). A `min_human_agreement` threshold key gates CI with a three-state rule: human_agreement key absent → silent skip (calibration is post-hoc; keeps cmd_judges-at-scoring-time and Harbor aggregates safe), perfect-agreement degenerate → pass, otherwise unavailable/below-floor → regression. Below n<5 the coefficient is suppressed and a raw agreement table is emitted instead. All outputs are labeled "agreement with a single human reviewer (n=X)" — never validated accuracy. Optional small attach_feedback.py change pushes verdicts as HUMAN-source MLflow assessments named {case}/{judge}/human. All 7 corrections from the V3-2 verdict are incorporated, plus the analogous V3-1 corrections (perfect-agreement degenerates pass; Harbor path scoped out by construction; no config.thresholds mutation; no Landis-Koch labels).
depends_on: WS1 (V3-1) agent_eval/reliability.py — HARD prerequisite, stdlib-only. Assumed interface: select_irr_metric(n_raters, varying_identity, complete_matrix, scale) -> (metric_name, rationale_str); cohen_kappa(ratings_a, ratings_b) -> (value_or_None, reason_str); krippendorff_alpha(units, level) -> (value_or_None, reason_str) where units is a list of per-unit rating lists and level in {nominal, ordinal, interval}; degenerate zero-variance matrices return (None, reason). WS6 isolates this contract behind one wrapper (compute_human_agreement in score.py) so a signature drift is a one-function fix.

No other workstream dependency: config.py needs no change (thresholds stay a raw dict, config.py:897 and :1451; validate_eval.py:809-818 only checks judge names — verified, per verdict correction #7).

changes.spec: Four edits, all prose (agent-enforced). (1) Step 0 argument table: add `--calibrate` flag — 'collect per-judge human verdicts BEFORE any judge scores or report content are shown (blind mode)'. This is the verdict correction #3 optional entry mode. (2) Step 2 (lines 44-55): when --calibrate is set, defer the analysis.md/report.html overview until after verdict collection; otherwise note that because /eval-run auto-opens report.html the user has typically already seen judge verdicts, so blind must be recorded false. Add an explicit instruction to determine and record the blind flag (true only if the user has seen neither report.html nor judge scores this session — ask if unsure) and the selection basis from the existing 'all cases, only failures, or specific cases?' answer (all|failures|manual). (3) Step 3 (lines 57-68): new sub-step 'Calibration verdicts (optional)' — offer once at walkthrough start; when accepted, reorder the per-case presentation to: output summary first, then elicit the human's verdict for each judge on that judge's own scale via AskUserQuestion (pass/fail for bool judges; an integer/float within score_range for numeric ones; 'skip' allowed per judge), and only THEN reveal judge scores, rationale, and pairwise results (correction #3: elicit-before-reveal). (4) Step 5 (lines 89-104): extend the review.yaml schema — keep `reviewer: "human"` (legacy coarse source field, correction #5 reconciliation), add `reviewer_id: "<identifier>"` (default 'human'), `blind: true|false`, `selection: all|failures|manual`, and `verdicts: {<case-dir-name>: {<judge_name>: <value-on-judge-scale>}}`; note keys must match case directory names exactly (same rule as feedback); document the forward path for multiple reviewers (a future verdicts_by_reviewer nesting — current flat form is single-reviewer, correction #5). Add Step 5b: run `python3 ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../eval-run/scripts/score.py calibration --run-id <id> --config <config>` when verdicts were collected (cross-skill invocation matches the existing ../eval-analyze pattern at lines 120/127), then optionally regenerate report.html. (5) Step 8: add `min_human_agreement` threshold suggestion and note verdicts flow to MLflow via push-feedback.

New 'Human calibration' section (after the pairwise section, ~line 2290) plus a detect_regressions branch and CLI wiring. (a) _load_review_verdicts(run_dir) -> (review: dict, verdicts: dict): loads review.yaml; exits 1 with a hint ('run /eval-review and collect verdicts') if the file or the verdicts key is missing; exits 1 with a structural message if verdicts is not a dict-of-dicts (review.yaml is agent-written YAML — validate loudly, never crash: verdict risk note). (b) _calibration_join(per_case, verdicts, judge_specs) -> dict {judge_name: {pairs: [(case_id, human, judge)], excluded: {skipped,errored,malformed,off_scale,unmatched}, warnings: [...]}} — pure, unit-testable. Join rules (correction #6, all named): compare against the REDUCED per_case value (per_case[case][judge]['value'] IS the _aggregate_samples reduction — majority for bool, median_low for numeric, score.py:1190-1240 — never stability.values); exclude value-None entries, distinguishing if:-skipped (no 'error' key, score.py:1555-1560) from errored (error key, score.py:1565-1571/1599-1601), each counted separately; verdict case key not in per_case -> 'unmatched' + stderr warning; judge name not in config judge_specs or not in the per_case row -> warning + skip; type harmonization: bool judge requires isinstance(h, bool) (else 'malformed'); numeric judge requires isinstance(h,(int,float)) and not isinstance(h,bool), and a declared score_range excludes off-scale human values ('off_scale', never clamped — mirrors _enforce_bounds policy); every exclusion shrinks n toward the floor and is reported. (c) _judge_scale(jc, pairs) -> 'nominal'|'ordinal'|'interval': feedback_type=='bool' or all-bool joined values -> nominal; integer score_range bounds (config.py:693 semantics) or all-int values -> ordinal; else interval. (d) compute_human_agreement(pairs, scale, floor=5) -> dict {metric, scale, value, reason, degenerate, agreement_raw, n, excluded, label, rationale}: deferred `from agent_eval.reliability import select_irr_metric, cohen_kappa, krippendorff_alpha` (single adaptation point for the WS1 contract); calls select_irr_metric(n_raters=2, varying_identity=False, complete_matrix=True, scale=scale) — Cohen's kappa is structurally valid HERE (exactly 2 fixed raters, complete matrix by construction of the join, nominal), alpha otherwise; nominal -> cohen_kappa(h_vec, j_vec); ordinal/interval -> krippendorff_alpha([[h,j],...], level=scale); agreement_raw = exact-match proportion, always present, labeled 'uncorrected'; n < floor -> value=None, reason='n=X below floor (5) — coefficient suppressed; raw agreement table only' (workstream requirement); WS1 degenerate (None, reason) -> value=None with degenerate='perfect_agreement' iff agreement_raw == 1.0 (V3-1 correction #1 analog); label='agreement with a single human reviewer (n=X)' (correction #5); no Landis-Koch adjectives anywhere. (e) cmd_calibration(args): load EvalConfig + summary.yaml (exit 1 'run judges first' if per_case/judges missing) + review; join; compute per judge; print a per-judge line (metric, value or suppression reason, n, uncorrected agreement, label) and, when suppressed, the raw pairs table rows; persist by loading summary, setting judges[name]['human_agreement']=result for each calibrated judge, then _merge_summary(run_id,'judges',judges_block) (correction #1 — the gate and report.py:1360-style agg reads live here) AND _merge_summary(run_id,'calibration',{reviewer, reviewer_id (fallback reviewer then 'human'), blind (absent->false, conservative), selection (absent->'unspecified'), n_total=len(per_case), n_reviewed, floor, judges:{name:{pairs:[{case,human,judge,match}], excluded}}}) for the run-level detail/raw tables (corrections #3/#4 recorded machine-readably); finally evaluate ONLY the min_human_agreement subset of config.thresholds via detect_regressions(judges_block, subset) and exit 1 on breach (mirrors cmd_judges; does not re-fire unrelated keys like min_win_rate). Note in a comment that a later `score.py judges` re-run wholesale rewrites summary['judges'] (score.py:2741-2744) and thus intentionally invalidates calibration — re-run calibration after re-scoring. (f) detect_regressions (score.py:2516-2587): new branch — if 'min_human_agreement' in threshold: ha=current.get('human_agreement'); if ha is absent entirely -> SILENT skip with a comment explaining the deliberate deviation from the configured-but-unavailable pattern (cmd_judges runs detect_regressions at scoring time before any review can exist, score.py:2767, and harbor/run.py:695 + harbor/results.py aggregates never carry the key — V3-1 corrections #2 analog); if ha dict: value None + degenerate=='perfect_agreement' -> pass (no regression); value None otherwise -> Regression(judge,'human_agreement', '>= T', 'n/a', ha['reason']); numeric value < T -> Regression with detail f'{metric} vs single human reviewer (n=X)'. (g) main(): add `calibration` subparser (--run-id required, --config required, --floor type=int default 5) + dispatch entry; args.run_id already passes _validate_path_segment (score.py:2934). No new third-party imports; module stays stdlib+yaml+agent_eval (house venv rules already satisfied: bootstrap at score.py:14, agent_eval symlink exists).

(a) _render_scoring_summary (1302-1475): after the stability bar block (1358-1364), read ha=agg.get('human_agreement'); if dict, append an annotation span to metric_val: numeric value -> 'κ=0.62 vs human (n=7)' (metric-name-appropriate symbol: kappa/alpha), title tooltip = label ('agreement with a single human reviewer (n=7)') + rationale from select_irr_metric + 'uncorrected agreement 0.83' (P8 reporting triple: metric, value, selection rationale); value None below floor -> 'human n=3 (<5 — no coefficient)'; degenerate -> 'human 100% raw (coefficient undefined — perfect agreement)'. Threshold column chain (1385-1393): add `elif "min_human_agreement" in thresh: thresh_str = f'≥ {thresh["min_human_agreement"]} vs human'` (the column is a representative bound; comment at 1384 says which is cosmetic). (b) New _render_calibration(summary) -> str, rendered via _wrap_section between Regressions and Shared Outputs in generate_report (2933-2935): returns '' when summary.get('calibration') is falsy; otherwise a 'Human Calibration' section with a metadata line (reviewer_id, n_reviewed/n_total, floor) and mandatory caveats — blind false/absent: 'verdicts were collected after judge results were visible (not blind)' (correction #3); selection != all: 'coefficients computed on a non-random subset (selection: failures) are prevalence-biased — kappa is prevalence-sensitive; interpret with caution' (correction #4); always: 'single human reviewer — no reliability estimate exists on the human anchor itself' (correction #5); then per-judge collapsible raw pairs tables (case / human / judge / match) — this is the required below-floor raw agreement table, rendered for every calibrated judge. (c) _render_per_case (2508-2710): derive verdicts=(review or {}).get('verdicts', {}) from the review dict already passed (loaded at report.py:3036); in the judge-results table loop (2601-2674), when verdicts.get(case_id,{}) has an entry for jname, append a badge to val_html: 'human: PASS'/'human: 4', CSS class pass-tinted on exact match with the judge value, warn-tinted on mismatch, title carrying reviewer_id; malformed (non-dict) verdict entries are ignored here (the calibration CLI already warned). (d) No _render_regressions change needed — it delegates to score.detect_regressions (1478-1487), so min_human_agreement breaches appear automatically; same for the log_results.py regressions_detected tag (log_results.py:49-66, 324-338).

In _push_feedback, after the human-review-comment block (lines 121-141): if args.source in ('human','all') and isinstance(review.get('verdicts'), dict): for case_id, jmap in verdicts (skip non-dict jmap with a stderr warning), for judge_name, value in jmap (skip None), call log_feedback(trace_id=..., name=f'{case_id}/{judge_name}/human', value=value, source_type='HUMAN', source_id=str(review.get('reviewer_id') or 'eval-review'), rationale='') for each trace_id, incrementing feedback_count — making MLflow-side judge-vs-human agreement queries joinable on the name convention ({case_id}/{judge_name} CODE vs {case_id}/{judge_name}/human HUMAN). The existing broadcast-to-all-traces behavior (find_run_traces ignores run_id) is explicitly out of scope per the proposal — same blast radius as the current human_review push. log_feedback (agent_eval/mlflow/experiment.py:272-287) already accepts bool/int/float values.

New test module following the test_threshold_consumers.py import pattern (sys.path.insert of repo root + skills/eval-run/scripts, then `from score import ...`). TestCalibrationJoin: join uses the REDUCED value not stability.values (per_case entry with value=True but stability.values=[True,False,True]); exclusion classes each counted and warned — if:-skipped (value None, no error key), errored (value None + error key), malformed (bool judge + numeric human verdict; numeric judge + string), off_scale (human 7 on score_range [1,5] → excluded, never clamped), unmatched (verdict for a case dir absent from per_case), unknown judge name skipped with warning. TestComputeHumanAgreement: bool judge n=8 with hand-computed Cohen's kappa (h=[T,T,T,T,F,F,F,F], j=[T,T,T,F,F,F,F,T] → po=0.75, pe=0.5, kappa=0.5), metric=='cohen_kappa', rationale non-empty, label=='agreement with a single human reviewer (n=8)'; int-scored judge → metric=='krippendorff_alpha', scale=='ordinal', value matches a direct reliability.krippendorff_alpha call on the same units (uses WS1's own fixtures as oracle); float → 'interval'; floor: n=4 → value None, reason mentions floor, agreement_raw still present; perfect agreement (all pairs identical) → value None, degenerate=='perfect_agreement', agreement_raw==1.0. TestGate (detect_regressions): human_agreement absent → no regression even with min_human_agreement configured (post-hoc rule); Harbor-shaped aggregate ({'values':..., 'mean':...} only, as harbor/results.py produces) → no regression; value 0.2 < 0.6 → regression with 'n=' detail; degenerate perfect → no regression; below-floor None → regression whose detail carries the floor reason; existing keys (min_mean etc.) unaffected. TestCmdCalibration (end-to-end on tmp_path with AGENT_EVAL_RUNS_DIR monkeypatched, SimpleNamespace args): writes summary['judges'][j]['human_agreement'] and summary['calibration'] (reviewer_id fallback chain, blind default false, selection default 'unspecified', pairs table content); SystemExit(1) when a configured min_human_agreement is breached, exit 0 otherwise; missing review.yaml → SystemExit(1) with hint; verdicts-as-list → SystemExit(1) structural message; subsequent _merge_summary(run_id,'judges',fresh_agg) drops human_agreement (documents the intended re-score invalidation). TestReportRendering (import report like test_threshold_consumers.py): _render_scoring_summary output contains 'vs human' and n; suppressed-coefficient text below floor; _render_calibration emits the not-blind and non-random-subset caveats and the raw pairs table, and returns '' without summary['calibration']; _render_per_case shows the human badge beside the judge value with mismatch tinting.

Add two rows to CASES (lines 32-43): ('min_human_agreement', {'q': {'mean': 4.0, 'scored_cases': 5, 'human_agreement': {'metric': 'cohen_kappa', 'value': 0.2, 'n': 6}}}, {'q': {'min_human_agreement': 0.6}}, True) and a clean variant (value 0.9 → False). The existing parametrized tests then mechanically verify CLI-gate/report-Regressions-table/MLflow-tag agreement for the new key with zero new test code — the drift this file exists to prevent.

Monkeypatch attach_feedback.find_run_traces (returns one fake trace) and attach_feedback.log_feedback (records calls); build a tmp run dir with review.yaml containing feedback + verdicts + reviewer_id. Assert: verdict entries pushed with name f'{case}/{judge}/human', source_type='HUMAN', source_id==reviewer_id; reviewer_id absent → source_id 'eval-review'; None values and non-dict case entries skipped; a review.yaml without verdicts produces exactly the pre-change call set (regression guard); --source judge does not push verdicts. Skip module with pytest.importorskip('mlflow') to match the script's import guard.

acceptance_criteria: `score.py calibration --run-id R --config eval.yaml` on a run whose review.yaml has verdicts writes human_agreement {metric, scale, value, reason, degenerate?, agreement_raw, n, excluded, label, rationale} under summary['judges'][<judge>] AND a run-level summary['calibration'] block {reviewer, reviewer_id, blind, selection, n_total, n_reviewed, floor, judges.<name>.pairs}; exits 1 iff a configured min_human_agreement is breached.

Metric selection is structural, via reliability.select_irr_metric: bool judge + complete joined matrix → cohen_kappa (the one valid Cohen design: 2 fixed raters); int-scale judge → krippendorff_alpha ordinal; float → interval; the rationale string is persisted and shown in the report tooltip.

Join correctness (verdict correction #6): comparison uses per_case[case][judge]['value'] (the _aggregate_samples reduction), never stability.values; value-None entries are excluded with skipped vs errored distinguished; malformed, off-scale (never clamped), and unmatched entries are excluded, counted in `excluded`, and warned to stderr; n reflects only surviving pairs.

n < 5 (default --floor): value is null, reason names the floor, no coefficient is printed or rendered, and the raw agreement table (case/human/judge/match) appears in both CLI output and the report's Human Calibration section.

Gate plumbing (verdict correction #1): `score.py regression` (which reads only summary['judges'], score.py:2856-2875) fires min_human_agreement after calibration; detect_regressions three-state rule holds — absent human_agreement key → no regression (so cmd_judges at scoring time and harbor/run.py:695 with stability-less harbor aggregates never false-positive), degenerate perfect agreement → no regression, numeric value below threshold or non-degenerate null → regression.
Every rendered/printed coefficient carries the label 'agreement with a single human reviewer (n=X)' (correction #5) and no Landis-Koch-style qualitative adjective appears anywhere.

report.html: Scoring Summary rows show the human-agreement annotation beside the stability bar; a Human Calibration section renders blind and selection caveats verbatim when blind is false/absent or selection != all (corrections #3/#4); Per-Case Details show the human verdict beside the judge verdict with match/mismatch tinting; the Regressions table shows min_human_agreement breaches (shared detector).

review.yaml schema in skills/eval-review/SKILL.md documents reviewer_id, blind, selection, verdicts; retains reviewer: 'human'; Step 3 instructs eliciting verdicts before revealing judge rationale; Step 0 documents --calibrate.

attach_feedback.py --source human|all pushes each verdict as a HUMAN-source assessment named {case_id}/{judge_name}/human with source_id = reviewer_id (fallback 'eval-review'); behavior is byte-identical when verdicts are absent.

No config.py or validate_eval.py changes; no new third-party dependency on the scoring path (grep score.py imports: stdlib + yaml + agent_eval only); reliability imported only inside compute_human_agreement.

open_questions: Below-floor gating policy: when min_human_agreement is configured and calibration ran but n < 5, the plan treats the suppressed coefficient as a regression (consistent with the existing configured-but-unavailable pattern, detail says 'review more cases'). The alternative is a silent pass until n reaches the floor. Which do you want? (Plan default: regression.)

Re-score invalidation: `score.py judges` re-runs wholesale rewrite summary['judges'] (score.py:2741-2744) and therefore drop human_agreement — the plan treats this as correct (new judge values invalidate old calibration; re-run `score.py calibration`, whose inputs in review.yaml survive). Confirm, or should cmd_judges preserve-and-flag stale calibration instead?

reviewer_id capture: should /eval-review actively ask who is reviewing (name/handle recorded in review.yaml and pushed to MLflow as source_id), or default silently to 'human' unless the user volunteers it? (Privacy vs multi-reviewer traceability.)
